title: Method for Determining Residual Total Suspended Solids in Sand Filters
author: Benítez, Muniz, et al.

steps.title: Collect upper filter bed layer
steps.instruction: Immediately after backwashing, sample the upper layer of the pressurized sand filter to assess residual solids.

steps.title: Remove upper 100 mm of sand
steps.instruction: Using a hand scoop, carefully remove all sand within the upper 100 mm of the filter bed and transfer it to a clean container; this single composite sample represents the entire sampled layer.

steps.title: Homogenize and dry sand
steps.instruction: Manually homogenize the collected sand by thorough hand‑mixing, then separate approximately 1 kg, place it in a forced‑air oven at 105 °C for 36 h (or until constant mass) to achieve complete moisture removal.

steps.title: Cool and store dried sand
steps.instruction: Allow the dried sand to cool to room temperature and store it in sealed containers until laboratory processing.

steps.title: Prepare extraction bottles
steps.instruction: For each 150 g sand subsample, transfer the sand into a 500 mL glass Stohlmann‑type bottle that has been washed with tap water and visually inspected for residues; add 200 mL distilled water (electrical conductivity < 5 µS cm⁻¹).

steps.title: Load bottles into shaker
steps.instruction: Place the sealed bottles vertically in a Wagner‑type soil dispersion shaker (TE‑160, Tecnalis, Brazil). Process three sample bottles simultaneously and add a fourth bottle containing only water to maintain mechanical balance; the shaker can hold up to eight bottles.

steps.title: Set shaker speed
steps.instruction: Adjust the shaker rotational speed to 15 rpm using the potentiometer and verify with a stopwatch; this speed matches the manual inversion protocol of Van Staden and Haarhoff.

steps.title: Execute five washing cycles
steps.instruction: Perform five consecutive extraction cycles, each consisting of adding water, agitating, and decanting the supernatant, then combining all supernatants into a single 1 L beaker.

substeps.instruction: Add 200 mL distilled water to the sand in the bottle (for the first cycle the water is already present).
Agitate the bottle in the shaker for 3 min at 15 rpm.
Remove the bottle, carefully decant the supernatant into a 1 L beaker, avoiding transfer of sand particles.
Add a fresh 200 mL of distilled water to the sand remaining in the bottle.
Repeat agitation (3 min) and decantation, adding the new supernatant to the same beaker.
Continue steps a–e until a total of five washing cycles have been completed; the combined suspension is used for TSSf determination.

steps.title: Manual extraction (optional)
steps.instruction: If a Wagner‑type shaker is unavailable, perform each washing cycle by completely inverting the bottle at least 20 times, allowing partial settling of sand after each inversion before the next inversion.
